questions.prompt: Money you keep for later instead of spending is called…
questions.explanation: Savings is money you put aside for later.

questions.prompt: A rainy-day fund is money for…
choices: Nothing at all, it just sits
questions.explanation: A rainy-day (emergency) fund covers surprises.

questions.prompt: You save ${a} each week. How much after {w} weeks?
questions.explanation: ${a} × {w} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Your jar has ${h}. You add ${a}. How much now?
questions.explanation: ${h} + ${a} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A toy costs ${p}. You have ${h}. How much more do you need?
questions.explanation: ${p} − ${h} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You need ${g} and save ${a} a week. How many weeks?
questions.explanation: ${g} ÷ ${a} = {ANSWER} weeks.

questions.prompt: Where is the SAFEST place to keep savings?
questions.explanation: Banks keep money safe and pay interest.

questions.prompt: Which is a good savings goal?
choices: Save $20 for a book in 5 weeks
Spend it all as soon as you get it
questions.explanation: Good goals are specific: how much and by when.

questions.prompt: You get ${a} allowance and save half. How much do you save?
questions.explanation: Half of ${a} is ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: If you save a little every week, your savings…
questions.explanation: Small amounts add up over time!

questions.prompt: When the bank pays you extra for keeping money there, that extra is called…
questions.explanation: Interest is money paid to you for saving.

questions.prompt: You save ${P}. The bank adds 10% in a year. How much interest?
questions.explanation: 10% of ${P} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You have ${P} and earn ${i} interest. How much in total?
questions.explanation: ${P} + ${i} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Which bank pays MORE interest on your savings each year?
questions.explanation: A higher percent means more interest.

questions.prompt: Interest that also earns interest is called…
questions.explanation: Compound interest = interest on your interest. It snowballs!

questions.prompt: Who ends up with more: Mia saves from age 10, Leo from age 30 (same amount each year)?
questions.explanation: Starting early gives your money more years to grow.

questions.prompt: $100 grows 10% one year, then 10% of the NEW amount the next year. How much after 2 years?
questions.explanation: $100 → $110 → $121. The second year earned $11 because interest earned interest!

questions.prompt: A money tree grows bigger when you…
choices: Leave the money in to grow
Take some money out every day
Spend all the interest it makes
questions.explanation: Leaving money in lets interest keep growing.

questions.prompt: Retirement is when people…
questions.explanation: Retirement is the time after a working career.

questions.prompt: Why do grown-ups save for retirement?
choices: To have money when they stop work
To pay for recess at school
Because the bank tells them to
To buy lots of candy today
questions.explanation: Without a paycheck, retirees live on savings.

questions.prompt: The BEST time to start saving for later is…
questions.explanation: The earlier you start, the more time money has to grow.

questions.prompt: Grandpa saved ${a} each year for {y} years. How much did he put in?
questions.explanation: ${a} × {y} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Some jobs add extra money to your retirement savings when you save. This is called…
questions.explanation: An employer match is free money added to your savings!

questions.prompt: You save ${a} and your job matches it dollar for dollar. How much goes in?
questions.explanation: ${a} + ${a} match = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Insurance helps you pay for…
questions.explanation: Insurance protects you from big unexpected costs.

questions.prompt: The small amount you pay each month for insurance is called a…
questions.explanation: A premium is the price of insurance.

questions.prompt: Which thing do families usually insure?
questions.explanation: We insure expensive things that would be hard to replace.

questions.prompt: Insurance costs ${p} a month. How much for {m} months?
questions.explanation: ${p} × {m} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Why is insurance worth it even if nothing bad happens?
choices: It protects you if something does
You always get all your money back
It is free, so there is no cost
questions.explanation: You pay a little to avoid a giant cost if something happens.

questions.prompt: A helmet and insurance are alike because both…
questions.explanation: Both are about safety and protection.

questions.prompt: A bike costs ${b}. Insurance costs ${p} for a year. If the bike is stolen, how much does insurance save you?
questions.explanation: Without insurance you lose ${b}; with it you only paid ${p}. You save ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: When you borrow money, you must…
questions.explanation: Borrowed money must be paid back.

questions.prompt: You borrow ${b} and pay back ${p}. How much extra did you pay?
questions.explanation: ${p} − ${b} = ${ANSWER} extra.

questions.prompt: Which loan is better for you?
questions.explanation: Paying back less extra is better.

questions.prompt: Extra money paid for borrowing is called…
questions.explanation: Interest is the cost of borrowing.

questions.prompt: You owe ${o} and pay ${a} a week. How many weeks to pay it off?
questions.explanation: ${o} ÷ ${a} = {ANSWER} weeks.

questions.prompt: Before borrowing, it is smart to ask…
choices: Can I pay it back on time?
Is the lender a funny person?
How soon can I borrow more?
questions.explanation: Only borrow what you can pay back.

questions.prompt: Paying a loan back FASTER usually means you pay…
questions.explanation: Less time owing = less interest.

questions.prompt: Giving money or time to help others is called…
questions.explanation: Charity helps people and causes.

questions.prompt: Before giving to a charity, it's smart to…
choices: Check that it’s real and trusted
Give to any stranger who asks online
Give away all of your money
Never ask any questions about it
questions.explanation: Check charities so your gift really helps.

questions.prompt: You have ${a} and give 10%. How much do you give?
questions.explanation: 10% of ${a} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Which is a way to give without money?
questions.explanation: Volunteering is giving your time and skills.

questions.prompt: Three friends give ${a} each to a food bank. How much in total?
questions.explanation: ${a} × 3 = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: At the hawker centre, chicken rice is $4 and noodles are $6. Which leaves more money in your wallet?
questions.explanation: $4 is less than $6, so chicken rice leaves $2 more.

questions.prompt: Lunch is ${l} and a drink is ${d}. You pay with ${p}. What change do you get?
You get $20. Which plan is most balanced?
choices: Save some, spend some, give some
Give it all to a stranger online
questions.explanation: Save, spend and give, a balanced plan!

questions.prompt: You want ${g}. You have ${h} and save ${a} a week. How many weeks?
questions.explanation: Still need ${g} − ${h}; ÷ ${a} = {ANSWER} weeks.

questions.prompt: If something bad is very unlikely AND cheap to fix, you…
choices: Probably don’t need insurance for it
Should worry about it all the time
Must borrow money to cover it now
questions.explanation: Insure the big, hard-to-pay surprises; small ones can come from savings.

questions.prompt: Your money tree earns 10% a year. Which grows it the MOST?
questions.explanation: The same $100 left for 5 years earns interest every year, and later years earn interest on earlier interest too.
questions.hint: Which one stays in the longest?

questions.prompt: A loan with a big fee and low interest might still cost…
choices: More than you think: check the TOTAL
Nothing, because the interest is low
Less than zero, the bank pays you
questions.explanation: Always compare the total amount you'll pay back.

questions.prompt: Money saved for retirement is meant to be used…
choices: When you are older and stop working
For snacks at the hawker centre
To pay a friend back next week
questions.explanation: Retirement savings are for later in life, when people stop working and no longer get a paycheck.

questions.prompt: You save ${P} and get 5% interest each year (simple). How much interest after {t} years?
questions.explanation: 5% of ${P} × {t} years = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Uncle Lim keeps 3 jars: Spend, Save, Give. Which jar is for a bike next summer?
questions.explanation: Money for a future goal goes in the Save jar.

questions.prompt: You raised ${a} for the animal shelter. A local shop doubles it! How much does the shelter get?
questions.explanation: ${a} × 2 = ${ANSWER}.
